perspective:
From Brandon Talayumptewa’s available perspective:

- I am Brandon Talayumptewa, an insurance agent.
- I met Benjamin Erickson for the first time in a professional setting. He came to me as an entrepreneur seeking business insurance advice.
- I was aware that Benjamin had limited formal education, so I was concerned about explaining complex insurance details clearly.
- In that first meeting, I explained comprehensive coverage, liabilities, assets, liability insurance as a safety net, a slip-and-fall example, and asset protection for inventory/equipment. Benjamin told me some terms were new, asked for an example, said my explanation simplified things, asked about assets, and thanked me for breaking it down.
- In a later meeting, I felt more confident that Benjamin could understand detailed information. I planned to discuss more complex policy details. I explained business interruption insurance and property insurance covering damages and theft. Benjamin said he had been reading up, that business interruption sounded crucial, and that comprehensive coverage was reassuring.
- At a casual lunch, I worried I was too caught up in details and wanted to keep discussions interesting. Benjamin said he appreciated my thoroughness but also enjoyed lighter moments. I told a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds. Benjamin responded with interest. I connected it to assessing risks and compared it to his business. Benjamin agreed.
- Pleased by Benjamin’s positive response, I decided to offer more support beyond insurance. I suggested strategic investments to lower premiums and upgrading security systems to protect assets and reduce insurance costs. Benjamin said he had not considered it, called it smart, and agreed to explore it.
- Encouraged by our rapport and mutual benefits, I felt optimistic and proposed a joint venture: co-developing a platform integrating risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin agreed, called it groundbreaking, said combining our expertise could set us apart, and suggested drafting initial plans. I agreed and suggested leveraging our strengths.

I do not have access to Benjamin’s private thoughts, internal personality information, or anything he did not say or show in our interactions.
